steps.caption: Start KRAB. Choose a deployment path; Custom combines runtime choices.
Select the architectures of your cluster nodes.
Choose the Kubernetes distribution used by your cluster.
The overview keeps every configuration section within reach.
Press F1 for contextual help on any screen.
Open Runtimes. Arrow keys navigate; checked entries are selected.
Space toggles a runtime and updates the live configuration panel.
Preview the generated, version-pinned Helm values before saving.
Save your configuration to a file you can edit or automate later.
Review the destination and confirm the save.
Create a starter configuration without opening the TUI.
Validate the configuration offline before generating values.
Generate the Helm values file using the same pinned catalog as the website.
The output includes its format, chart version, and deployment path. Review it before deploying.
Start with the builder. The header gives you documentation, theme, and release choices.
Choose Custom to combine runtime and hardware paths, or start with a vendor path.
The configuration page starts with target architectures and the Kubernetes distribution.
Choose the architecture of your target nodes.
Select the Kubernetes distribution used by your cluster.
Choose a runtime. The highlighted option is QEMU.
Select the runtime you want to install. KRAB checks the architecture coverage as you choose.
Review the version-pinned Helm command and generated values before deploying.
Export the same configuration to continue in your terminal.
Download values for Helm, or export krab.json to keep working in the TUI and CLI.
